title: San Francisco Crime Data Story
text:
Crime in San Francisco
This is a data-driven look at crime in San Francisco using police department reports from 2003 to the present.



Crime Trends Over Time


Show code
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load both datasets
file1 = r"C:\Users\mich0\Downloads\Police_Department_Incident_Reports__Historical_2003_to_May_2018.csv"
file2 = r"C:\Users\mich0\Downloads\Police_Department_Incident_Reports__2018_to_Present_20250204.csv"

df1 = pd.read_csv(file1)
df2 = pd.read_csv(file2)

# Combine both
df = pd.concat([df1, df2], ignore_index=True)

# Normalize column name (older data may differ slightly)
category_col = 'Incident Category' if 'Incident Category' in df.columns else 'Category'

# Filter for drug-related incidents
df = df[df[category_col].str.upper().str.contains('DRUG|NARCOTIC', na=False)]

# Extract year
df['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Incident Date'], errors='coerce')
df = df.dropna(subset=['Date'])
df['Year'] = df['Date'].dt.year

# Count per year
yearly_counts = df.groupby('Year').size()

# Plot it
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
yearly_counts.plot(kind='bar', color='purple', edgecolor='black')
plt.title("Number of Drug/Narcotic Incidents per Year (2003–2024)")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Number of Incidents")
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
